newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank mulls "interest rate intervention".
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank mulls "interest rate intervention".

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said it was considering some type of "interest rate intervention" after all bids were rejected as too high in a seven-day reverse repurchase tender on Monday.

"The truth is that we are considering some possible interest rate intervention...but our policy has not changed for now," Peter Andresic, head of the NBS Open Market Operation Department, told Reuters after the tender was completed.
The NBS earlier said it had rejected all bids, totalling 500 million crowns, in the seven-day reverse repo tender to drain liquidity.

According to official NBS figures, banks had a liquidity surplus at the beginning of a new minimum reserve period on Monday with reserve demands fulfilled at 104.27 percent as of the end of last week.
The NBS held the tender to drain an unspecified volume of liquidity from the interbank money market on Monday morning, with no fixed minimum rate.

"Bid rates were high from our point of view, higher than those accepted in the previous tenders, therefore we rejected them," Andresic said, but declined to specify what rates the central bank had wanted.
Rates in the NBS's last successful seven-day reverse repo tender on Friday fell to 14.6 percent from 17.3 percent more than a week prior, as commercial banks bid the market down.
The NBS said last week that the drop in yield in the tender should be seen as a signal to the market.

The downward signal came two days after the Slovak government decided to participate in the central bank's board meetings, prompting analysts to voice concerns over the bank's independence, and raising expectations of an interest rate cut.
